newsitem.title: FRANCE: Last Mastroianni partner in battle mood at Cannes.
newsitem.headline: Last Mastroianni partner in battle mood at Cannes.

text.p: Marcello Mastroianni's last companion was in fighting mood after her filmed portrait of the late Italian legend, unveiled at the Cannes festival, fuelled an ugly dispute over his legacy.

"Enough of this mindless polemic. For the love of Marcello," Anna Maria Tato bristled in her first Cannes interview with reporters, as her clash with other women linked to the stereotype Latin lover overshadowed her screening of "Mi ricordo si io mi ricordo" (I Remember).

Mastroianni's partner for the last 22 years of his life ignited a storm in March, three months after he died, by telling industry bible Variety in March that a codicil to his will gave her control over marketing his artistic legacy.
She will decide how his films are used, where his interviews and photographs appear and where videos of his television and stage appearances are shown.

"It's simple, I have the same role as Mazarine, the daughter of the late (French) president Francois Mitterrand," Tato said as she tore bits off a cheese sandwich and drank champagne at a mid-afternoon lunch.

French actress Catherine Deneuve, industry sources say, unsuccessfully put pressure on Cannes organisers to keep the Mastroianni film away from the festival. Chiara, her daughter by Mastroianni, has questioned the authenticity of the codicil.
Stung by the reaction, Tato justified herself: "I was the woman who spent the most time with him. He knew me well, this film is all love. I don't want to be the widow who controls everything.

"People launched a slander campaign without even seeing one shot, people said that I filmed the agony of Marcello. In this film Marcello is proud, handsome, elegant, funny and so intelligent," said Tato, a feature film director who has made documentaries on Woody Allen and Vittorio Gassman, among others.

The six hours of footage about his life and career, which begin with a monologue by a silhouetted Mastroianni, have been cut to two hours for Cannes and will be shown in a four-hour version at the Venice festival this autumn.

Insights into Mastroianni include him reciting a Chekhov monologue -- there is no known film of any of his theatrical appearances -- and an audition for a film Federico Fellini never made ("Mastroianni Returns") in which he plays the cello.
Mastroianni always liked to be seen working and the shooting took place during filming of Manoel de Oliveira's "Journey to the Beginning of the World", also featured at this year's Cannes festival.
Tato said she had no plans to lift the veil in the lengthier version on Mastroianni's private life, which included relationships with Sophia Loren, Silvana Mangano and Faye Dunaway.

"He was so much at ease during filming because he felt protected, sheltered from indiscreet questions. There are no questions on his private life, he has been massacred for that in the press," she said.
The project was born by chance. Mastroianni had been inundated with profile requests from foreign television networks and turned to her a few days later to suggest they do a profile together.
"I said only with 35mm film, and he said only in Portugal. Those were our only conditions," Tato recalled.
